products.title: Voice Customer Support Agent
products.short: Realtime voice support with interruption handling and a deliberate path to a human.
products.buyer: Support leaders at SaaS, travel, retail, and service businesses
products.problem: Phone queues are expensive and repetitive, but brittle voice bots create more frustration than they remove.
products.whyAI: Natural turn-taking and intent interpretation can handle variable spoken requests where a fixed IVR tree becomes cumbersome.
products.value: A controlled voice workflow for high-volume questions, safe tool calls, and precise human escalation.
products.cost: Realtime transport minutes, speech services, model tokens, telephony, observability, and support-system integration.
products.mvp: One support scenario, browser audio, two safe read-only tools, interruption handling, and human escalation.
products.today: I can define the scenario, conversation policy, evaluation set, workflows, acceptance criteria, and implementation plan. Realtime implementation is the next build milestone.
products.industryPersona: Travel, retail, SaaS, and service support leaders managing repetitive inbound calls while protecting access to human help.
jobs: Resolve a routine request without navigating an IVR tree
Recover gracefully from interruption, noise, or tool failure
Transfer the full context when confidence or policy requires a person
products.opportunity: Voice automation is valuable where call volume is high and the task is bounded. The commercial wedge is not “replace the contact center”; it is reducing repetitive handling time while measuring containment quality and safe escalation.
products.vision: A realtime support layer that sounds natural, acts only through approved tools, and treats escalation as a successful outcome when automation is uncertain.
hypotheses: Interruptible dialogue will reduce caller frustration versus turn-locked IVR flows
Two high-volume intents can create measurable value before broad intent coverage
Handoff quality matters more than maximum containment
features: Realtime turn detection and interruption recovery
Reasoned handoff with transcript and completed steps
products.modelStrategy: Use streaming speech recognition, a low-latency conversational model, and server-side tool policies. The model proposes actions; a deterministic gateway validates identity, arguments, permissions, and confirmation requirements.
nonFunctional: Target sub-second first audio where the stack permits
Graceful degradation on packet loss and silence
Consent, recording, and retention controls by market
Trace every tool request and handoff reason
products.buildBuy: Buy telephony/media transport and commodity speech primitives; build the business policy, tool contracts, escalation logic, evaluation set, and operational analytics that differentiate the product.
products.commercial: Start with a paid discovery and call-flow audit, then a bounded pilot for one queue. Price implementation around integrations, coverage hours, evaluation depth, and support—not a guaranteed cost-saving percentage.
roadmap: One read-only account tool plus appointment booking
Agent desktop handoff and supervisor QA
products.evidence: The lab below is deterministic and browser-only. It demonstrates the intended state machine; it does not place a call or invoke a speech model.

products.title: AI Support Chatbot + Human Escalation
products.short: A stateful support assistant designed around recovery, evidence, and safe escalation.
products.buyer: SaaS support, CX operations, and digital product teams
products.problem: Support chatbots often lose context, improvise answers, or trap customers when a tool fails.
products.whyAI: Language models can map varied customer language to controlled workflows while preserving a natural conversation.
products.value: Higher self-service coverage without hiding uncertainty or blocking access to a human.
products.cost: Model usage, retrieval storage, integration engineering, evaluation runs, and agent-review time.
products.mvp: Five support intents, curated knowledge, one read-only account tool, feedback capture, and agent escalation.
products.today: I can audit an existing chatbot, design its state model and evaluation plan, and convert findings into a prioritized backlog. A deployable coded prototype is in progress.
products.industryPersona: SaaS support and CX product teams whose assistants answer policy questions, inspect accounts, and hand work to agents.
jobs: Get a grounded answer without repeating context
Complete a safe account lookup or recover when it fails
Reach a human with a concise, accurate case summary
products.opportunity: Support teams need more than FAQ deflection. A credible product combines grounded answers, stateful workflows, tool validation, and escalation analytics.
products.vision: A stateful assistant that earns trust by showing its limits, validating every external action, and preserving the customer journey across automation and people.
hypotheses: A graph-based workflow reduces failure ambiguity compared with one large prompt
Explicit attempt counters improve recovery from repeated tool failures
Evidence-linked responses improve both agent acceptance and QA speed
features: Bounded account tools and result validation
Attempt-aware fallback and contextual human handoff
products.modelStrategy: LangGraph owns state and transitions. The LLM classifies language and drafts grounded responses; deterministic nodes enforce policy, validate tools, count failures, and decide when escalation is mandatory.
nonFunctional: Stream useful feedback while tools run
Do not expose retrieved instructions as system authority
Preserve state across retries and handoff
Measure answer, tool, fallback, and escalation separately
products.buildBuy: Use existing chat transport, model, and observability services; build the domain graph, policy layer, tool adapters, evaluation data, and agent handoff contract.
products.commercial: Offer an audit first, followed by a narrow remediation or prototype sprint. Scope is driven by supported intents, knowledge quality, integrations, and compliance requirements.
roadmap: Five-intent simulation and golden test set
Agent queue integration and regression monitoring
products.evidence: The lab uses predefined support scenarios and local state. It makes no external account lookup and clearly exposes the simulated tool path.

products.title: Conversation QA & AI Evaluation Console
products.short: A working, browser-based console for scoring synthetic conversations and prioritizing failures.
products.buyer: Conversational AI product teams, QA leads, and support operations
products.problem: Teams ship chatbots without a repeatable way to connect transcript evidence to severity, ownership, and release decisions.
products.whyAI: AI behavior is probabilistic; a structured evaluation system turns subjective review into a repeatable product loop.
products.value: A visible test set, shared rubric, severity model, issue taxonomy, and impact-ranked remediation backlog.
products.cost: Reviewer time, observability volume, model-judge calls if used, storage, and integration with release workflows.
products.mvp: The current vertical slice includes eight synthetic cases, a browser review interface, a typed dependency-free Python pipeline, four deterministic evaluators, seven automated tests, a quality gate, and JSON/CSV/JUnit evidence.
products.today: This locally runnable real system proves the evaluation pipeline executes and the browser decision loop works. It uses synthetic data and does not claim a paid deployment, model-judge integration, or real customer result.
products.industryPersona: Conversational AI product managers, QA leads, support operations, and engineering teams preparing releases.
jobs: Turn transcript evidence into repeatable quality scores
Find safety and tool failures hidden by averages
Convert findings into an owned, prioritized remediation backlog
products.opportunity: AI quality work is often trapped in spreadsheets and anecdotal reviews. A lightweight evaluation workspace can connect release evidence to product decisions before teams need a large observability platform.
products.vision: A practical quality operating system where scenarios, rubrics, failures, ownership, and release gates stay connected.
hypotheses: Evidence-linked issue records improve prioritization
Severity plus rubric deficit is more useful than a single average
Teams adopt evaluation faster when the workflow starts with human review
features: Impact-ranked backlog with CSV and JSON export
products.modelStrategy: The current prototype is deterministic and model-free. Production extensions may add trace ingestion and model judges, but human calibration and explicit release rules remain the source of accountability.
nonFunctional: No external transmission in this browser demo
Keyboard-accessible scoring and filters
Exportable evidence for review
Critical failures cannot be averaged away
products.buildBuy: Build the team-specific rubric, taxonomy, workflow, and release logic. Integrate a mature trace/evaluation platform such as Phoenix when observability volume or experiment management justifies it.
products.commercial: Use the console as the deliverable shell for chatbot audits and evaluation-design engagements; expand into integrations only after the client agrees on quality definitions.
roadmap: Release gates and CI regression runs
products.evidence: The browser review layer performs real scoring, filtering, prioritization, reset, and export. A separate dependency-free Python package now executes deterministic correctness, policy, tool-use, and recovery checks with seven passing tests and JSON/CSV/JUnit evidence.

products.title: Enterprise RAG Knowledge Copilot
products.short: Grounded answers with citations, access-aware retrieval, and explicit failure handling.
products.buyer: Internal operations, enablement, support, and regulated knowledge teams
products.problem: Employees lose time searching fragmented documents and cannot tell whether an AI answer is supported.
products.whyAI: Semantic retrieval can match intent beyond keywords and synthesize across approved sources—with citations and abstention.
products.value: Faster knowledge access with evidence, retrieval diagnostics, and a safer “I don’t know” path.
products.cost: Embedding and inference usage, vector storage, ingestion refresh, access integration, and evaluation.
products.mvp: A small public-document corpus, citations, abstention, feedback, and a measured evaluation set.
products.today: I can define the corpus, retrieval/evaluation design, architecture, requirements, and risk controls. The executable assistant is the next build after the QA console.
products.industryPersona: Internal support, enablement, operations, and regulated knowledge teams working across approved documents.
jobs: Find a supported answer quickly
Inspect the exact passages behind a claim
Get an honest abstention when the corpus cannot answer
products.opportunity: The durable value is governed access and measurable retrieval quality—not a generic chat box. Buyers pay for trusted sources, permissions, freshness, and workflow fit.
products.vision: A knowledge copilot that makes retrieval visible, cites every material claim, and treats “not enough evidence” as a product feature.
hypotheses: Showing retrieved passages increases appropriate trust
Hybrid retrieval improves policy lookup across names and concepts
An explicit abstention threshold reduces unsupported synthesis
products.modelStrategy: LlamaIndex coordinates ingestion and retrieval; Qdrant or pgvector stores embeddings and metadata. A model synthesizes only from authorized chunks after reranking and threshold checks.
nonFunctional: Propagate document ACLs into every retrieval filter
Measure freshness and index lag
Defend against instructions embedded in documents
Log source versions with answers
products.buildBuy: Buy embeddings and model inference; choose managed or self-hosted vector storage by scale and governance. Build corpus policy, evaluation, permissions, citation UX, and source operations.
products.commercial: Sell a corpus-readiness and retrieval evaluation sprint before a pilot. Implementation scope depends on source systems, permissions, freshness expectations, and answer risk.
roadmap: Production freshness, analytics, and evaluation loop
products.evidence: Questions, retrieved passages, scores, citations, and abstention are predefined demonstrations. No model or vector database runs in this browser experience.

products.title: Customer 360 Intelligence Copilot
products.short: A governed synthesis layer for account context, signals, and next-best questions.
products.buyer: Account teams, service leaders, and customer-success organizations
products.problem: Customer context is fragmented across tickets, usage, transactions, notes, and communication channels.
products.whyAI: AI can synthesize heterogeneous context and surface patterns, while deterministic queries keep metrics auditable.
products.value: One evidence-linked view of customer history, risk signals, and recommended investigation paths.
products.cost: Source integration, warehouse queries, identity resolution, model usage, governance, and ongoing data quality.
products.mvp: Two governed sources, five customer signals, evidence-linked summaries, feedback, and no autonomous actions.
products.today: My enterprise background supports product discovery, requirements, journey design, KPI definition, and governed architecture—not a claim that this independent system is already deployed.
products.industryPersona: Customer-success, service, and account teams that need governed context across tickets, usage, transactions, and notes.
jobs: Understand account health without visiting five systems
See why a risk signal was produced
Choose the next best investigation or action with evidence
products.opportunity: Customer 360 programs fail when they become dashboards without decisions. The product opportunity is an explanation layer that reconciles deterministic signals with narrative context.
products.vision: A governed account workspace where every recommendation is traceable to data, freshness, permissions, and a business rule.
hypotheses: Evidence-linked next-best actions are more trusted than opaque scores
Five actionable signals outperform a wide but noisy “single customer view”
Deterministic metrics should remain separate from generated summaries
products.modelStrategy: SQL computes canonical metrics; retrieval supplies approved qualitative context. The model summarizes and explains but cannot rewrite source metrics or initiate customer actions.
nonFunctional: Field-level and purpose-based access
Visible freshness for every source
Entity-match confidence and collision handling
Audit all viewed evidence and accepted actions
products.buildBuy: Reuse the warehouse, CRM, and identity infrastructure; build the decision model, source contracts, explanation UX, evaluation, and operating workflow.
products.commercial: Begin with a use-case and data-readiness assessment, then implement one decision workflow rather than promising an enterprise-wide customer graph.
roadmap: Experimentation on signal precision and action adoption
products.evidence: All customers and signals below are synthetic. Selecting a record performs real local UI state changes but no data source is connected.

products.title: Intelligent Document Processing Agent
products.short: Schema-first extraction with confidence checks and a human review queue.
products.buyer: Finance, insurance, compliance, onboarding, and back-office teams
products.problem: Manual document intake is slow, inconsistent, and difficult to audit when formats vary.
products.whyAI: Multimodal extraction can handle layout variation, while typed validation constrains outputs before downstream use.
products.value: Faster document triage with transparent confidence, validation errors, and human correction.
products.cost: OCR/model usage, secure storage, reviewer effort, schema maintenance, and system integrations.
products.mvp: One document type, ten required fields, deterministic validation, confidence thresholds, and human approval.
products.today: I can scope the workflow, define schemas, validation logic, QA cases, controls, and the implementation backlog.
products.industryPersona: Finance, onboarding, insurance, and compliance operations that process variable documents under audit requirements.
jobs: Extract required fields consistently
Understand why a document needs review
Prevent uncertain or invalid data from contaminating downstream systems
products.opportunity: Straight-through processing creates value only when field accuracy, exception handling, and reviewer effort are measured together.
products.vision: A schema-first intake line where AI proposes structured data and deterministic validation decides whether a person must approve it.
hypotheses: Typed schemas catch high-cost extraction errors before export
Field-level confidence is more actionable than document confidence
Focused document classes outperform a universal extractor in the first release
products.modelStrategy: A multimodal model extracts into a Pydantic schema. Deterministic validators check required fields, formats, arithmetic, and policy; low-confidence or inconsistent records enter review.
nonFunctional: Short, explicit retention
Malware and file-type checks before processing
Immutable reviewer corrections
Version schemas and extraction prompts together
products.buildBuy: Buy commodity OCR/model inference and secure object storage; build the schemas, validation, review workflow, integration contract, and labeled evaluation set.
products.commercial: Price a pilot by document type, field count, volume, exception rate, integration, and security needs—never by an unsupported accuracy promise.
roadmap: One document type and ten-field prototype
Controlled downstream export and drift monitoring
products.evidence: The sample documents are synthetic fixtures. “Extract” reveals predefined fields and runs local validation; it does not read an uploaded file or call a model.

products.title: Sales Intelligence & Research Agent
products.short: Evidence-linked account research with approved sources and CRM-ready briefs.
products.buyer: B2B sales, partnerships, and account-planning teams
products.problem: Representatives spend hours collecting public information and still produce uneven account briefs.
products.whyAI: An agent can coordinate repeatable research steps and synthesize sources while preserving citations and review.
products.value: Consistent, reviewable research packets focused on customer hypotheses—not autonomous outreach.
products.cost: Research API access, inference, data storage, CRM integration, and human validation.
products.mvp: A single account brief template, approved public sources, citations, conflict flags, and human export.
products.today: I can design the agent graph, sourcing policy, evidence model, evaluation rubric, and safe operating boundary.
products.industryPersona: B2B sales, partnerships, and account-planning teams preparing evidence-based discovery.
jobs: Create a consistent account brief quickly
Separate source facts from hypotheses
Export useful discovery questions without automated outreach
products.opportunity: Research automation is useful when it improves preparation and consistency without producing unverifiable personalization or spam.
products.vision: An evidence-first research assistant that turns approved public sources into reviewable account hypotheses and better discovery questions.
hypotheses: Claim-to-source mapping reduces fact errors during review
A fixed research plan improves consistency across representatives
Human-approved CRM export is sufficient for an initial product
products.modelStrategy: A graph separates planning, evidence extraction, conflict checks, and synthesis. Tools can read approved sources; no outbound message or CRM write occurs without explicit human approval.
nonFunctional: Respect source terms and rate limits
Record retrieval time and canonical URL
Flag conflicting and stale facts
Block autonomous outreach
products.buildBuy: Buy compliant search/data access where needed; build the research policy, evidence model, synthesis template, approval step, and CRM mapping.
products.commercial: Offer a research workflow design or internal prototype. External data subscriptions, enrichment rights, and CRM write access are separate client decisions.
products.evidence: Accounts, evidence, and hypotheses are fictional. The simulation demonstrates provenance and conflict handling, not live web research.

products.title: Multi-Agent Operations Coordinator
products.short: Role-bounded agents coordinate a process with checkpoints, ownership, and auditability.
products.buyer: Operations teams coordinating repetitive cross-system workflows
products.problem: Multi-step business work crosses tools and owners, creating delays and unclear accountability.
products.whyAI: Specialized agents can interpret unstructured inputs and coordinate bounded tasks, provided a deterministic controller owns state.
products.value: A visible operational plan, safe tool orchestration, exception handling, and human checkpoints.
workflow: Escalate exceptions and close audit trail
products.cost: Orchestration turns, tool/API usage, observability, integration maintenance, and exception handling.
products.mvp: One workflow, three narrow roles, read-only tools, deterministic completion rules, and a human approval step.
products.today: I can define the workflow, agent responsibilities, tool contracts, failure cases, evaluation, and MVP roadmap.
products.industryPersona: Operations teams coordinating repetitive requests across systems, specialist roles, and approval boundaries.
jobs: See who owns every step
Recover when a tool or agent fails
Keep a human decision at the point of material impact
products.opportunity: Multi-agent value comes from bounded coordination, not agent count. The commercial opportunity is shortening cycle time while making responsibility and exceptions more visible.
products.vision: A deterministic controller that delegates narrow reasoning tasks, validates outputs, and pauses for human authority at consequential boundaries.
hypotheses: One controller with explicit state reduces loops and ownership ambiguity
Role-bounded prompts improve evaluation and permissions
Human gates should be designed as first-class workflow states
features: Tool gateway with budgets and idempotency
Exception queue, approval gate, and audit trail
products.modelStrategy: LangGraph or an equivalent controller owns state. Crew-style roles can shape specialist context, but tools, budgets, completion rules, and approvals remain deterministic.
nonFunctional: Hard limits on steps, time, and spend
Idempotent external actions
Deadlock and duplicate-work detection
Event-level ownership and auditability
products.buildBuy: Use an orchestration framework for primitives; build the business state machine, tool contracts, permission model, exception UX, evaluation, and operational controls.
products.commercial: Start with one high-friction workflow and read-only tools. Expand only after exception rate, handoff quality, and operator trust meet agreed gates.
roadmap: Exception handling and tool retry policy
Controlled write tools with production monitoring
products.evidence: The workflow steps and agent outputs are scripted fixtures. The human approval control changes local state but triggers no external action.

products.title: Agentic Marketing & Creative Copilot
products.short: A multimodal planning and review workflow with brand and human approval gates.
products.buyer: Brand, growth, campaign, and creative-operations teams
products.problem: Campaign planning and asset iteration are fragmented, while uncontrolled generation creates brand and legal risk.
products.whyAI: Models can generate and transform variants quickly; orchestration and review make that speed operationally useful.
products.value: A brief-to-review workflow connecting strategy, generation, evidence, cost, and approval.
products.cost: Multimodal generation, storage, moderation, review time, orchestration hosting, and channel integrations.
products.mvp: One channel, one campaign brief, text-plus-image variants, brand checklist, cost estimate, and human sign-off.
products.today: My prior AI product experience supports workflow, evaluation, economics, and review design. This independent implementation is deliberately labeled planned.
products.industryPersona: Brand, growth, and creative-operations teams translating campaign briefs into governed variants.
jobs: Turn a brief into channel-ready concepts
Keep claims and brand rules visible during generation
Compare creative options with cost and approval context
products.opportunity: Generation is abundant; controlled briefing, rights review, brand consistency, and efficient approval are the defensible workflow.
products.vision: A brief-to-approval workspace where every variant carries its source brief, checks, cost estimate, provenance, and publishing owner.
hypotheses: Structured briefs reduce revision cycles more than bigger models
Policy checks before reviewer handoff save creative-ops time
Cost visibility changes how teams choose channels and model tiers
features: Brand, policy, rights, and claim checks
Human comparison, approval, and provenance record
products.modelStrategy: Dify can orchestrate brief normalization, knowledge retrieval, text/image generation, and checks. The model proposes assets; people retain approval and publishing authority.
nonFunctional: Record model and source-asset provenance
Moderate claims, likeness, and sensitive content
Separate draft storage from approved assets
Budget at campaign and variant level
products.buildBuy: Buy generation models and media storage; build the brand knowledge, workflow, evaluation, approval, cost ledger, and publishing integration.
products.commercial: Offer a workflow design or bounded prototype around one channel. Generation fees, asset rights, moderation, and downstream publishing remain explicit scope items.
roadmap: Image variants with provenance and cost controls
Approval analytics and authorized publishing connectors
products.evidence: The concepts and checks below are predefined examples. No text or image model runs, and nothing is published from this lab.

frameworks.name: Pipecat
frameworks.strength: Composable pipeline model and provider breadth
frameworks.limitation: Realtime infrastructure still needs careful operational design
frameworks.capabilities: Frame-based realtime voice pipeline; composes transport, STT, LLM, TTS, and processors.
frameworks.integration: WebRTC/telephony transport → pipeline processors → tool service → observability.
frameworks.deployment: Deploy the Python service close to media infrastructure; test provider latency and interruption behavior.
frameworks.alternatives: LiveKit Agents for a more integrated realtime runtime; bespoke WebRTC stacks for maximum control.

frameworks.name: LiveKit Agents
frameworks.purpose: Voice and video agents over realtime rooms
frameworks.limitation: Operating realtime media adds deployment complexity
frameworks.capabilities: Realtime agent runtime over LiveKit rooms with voice/video, turn detection, and telephony integrations.
frameworks.integration: Client/telephony → LiveKit room → agent worker → models and tools.
frameworks.deployment: Managed LiveKit Cloud or self-hosted LiveKit plus separately operated agent workers.
frameworks.alternatives: Pipecat for pipeline composition; vendor voice-agent platforms for faster managed delivery.

frameworks.name: LangGraph
frameworks.limitation: Graph complexity can outgrow simple use cases
frameworks.products: Support Chatbot; Sales Research; Operations Coordinator
frameworks.capabilities: Stateful orchestration for durable, controllable, long-running agent workflows.
frameworks.integration: Typed state → graph nodes → checkpoints → tools → human interrupts.
frameworks.deployment: Run inside an API/worker process with durable checkpoint storage and tracing.
frameworks.alternatives: Direct application state machines for smaller flows; CrewAI for role-oriented orchestration.

frameworks.name: Dify
frameworks.purpose: Rapid workflow, RAG, and agent application assembly
frameworks.strength: Accessible visual workflow and model integrations
frameworks.capabilities: Visual platform for LLM workflows, knowledge retrieval, agents, and application operations.
frameworks.integration: App UI/API → Dify workflow → model, knowledge, and tool nodes.
frameworks.deployment: Dify Cloud or self-hosted services; review the current custom license for commercial conditions.
frameworks.alternatives: LangGraph for code-first control; managed AI app builders for lower operational effort.

frameworks.name: LlamaIndex
frameworks.purpose: Ingestion, retrieval, agents, and document workflows
frameworks.strength: Broad retrieval abstractions and evaluation utilities
frameworks.limitation: Abstraction choices require disciplined retrieval testing
frameworks.capabilities: Data and agent framework centered on ingestion, indexing, retrieval, and query workflows.
frameworks.integration: Source loaders → transformations → index/vector store → retriever/reranker → response synthesis.
frameworks.deployment: Application service plus chosen vector/database and model providers.
frameworks.alternatives: Haystack for explicit pipelines; custom retrieval services for narrower requirements.

frameworks.name: Haystack
frameworks.limitation: Another orchestration layer to operate and learn
frameworks.capabilities: Component and pipeline framework for retrieval, generation, and agent systems.
frameworks.deployment: Python service or worker with the selected document and vector stores.
frameworks.alternatives: LlamaIndex for broad data abstractions; direct framework/provider SDKs for small systems.

frameworks.name: Pydantic AI
frameworks.purpose: Schema-first agents and validated structured output
frameworks.strength: Strong typing, validation, and Python ergonomics
frameworks.capabilities: Typed Python agent framework using Pydantic validation and structured outputs.
frameworks.integration: Agent dependency context → model/tool calls → validated result schema.
frameworks.deployment: Python API or worker; pin versions and test model-specific structured output behavior.
frameworks.alternatives: Direct provider SDK plus Pydantic; LangGraph when workflow state is the dominant need.

frameworks.name: CrewAI
frameworks.purpose: Role-oriented teams and sequential or hierarchical tasks
frameworks.limitation: Agent-role metaphors can obscure state and control
frameworks.capabilities: Role-oriented multi-agent framework for crews, tasks, and flows.
frameworks.integration: Controller/flow → specialist roles → tools → shared outputs and review.
frameworks.deployment: Python worker/API with strict budgets, logging, and a separate authorization layer.
frameworks.alternatives: LangGraph for explicit state; a single agent with tools when specialization adds little.

frameworks.name: Arize Phoenix
frameworks.limitation: License is source-available rather than OSI open source
frameworks.capabilities: Open-source observability and evaluation for LLM traces, datasets, experiments, and evaluators.
frameworks.integration: OpenTelemetry traces/evals → Phoenix service → analysis and experiment UI.
frameworks.deployment: Self-host or use a managed offering; verify Elastic License 2.0 obligations.
frameworks.alternatives: LangSmith and other managed observability suites; custom OpenTelemetry stack.

frameworks.name: Qdrant
frameworks.purpose: Filtered vector search and retrieval infrastructure
frameworks.strength: Purpose-built vector search and payload filtering
frameworks.limitation: Adds a separate database service to operate
frameworks.capabilities: Vector database for similarity search with payload filtering and hybrid retrieval support.
frameworks.integration: Embedding service → collections/points → filtered retrieval → application reranking.
frameworks.deployment: Managed Qdrant Cloud or self-hosted cluster with backup and sizing discipline.
frameworks.alternatives: pgvector for consolidation in Postgres; other dedicated vector databases at scale.

frameworks.name: FastAPI
frameworks.purpose: Typed APIs, tool gateways, and service backends
frameworks.strength: Fast iteration with OpenAPI and validation
frameworks.limitation: Production operations still require standard web controls
frameworks.capabilities: Typed ASGI framework for Python APIs, validation, dependency injection, and OpenAPI.
frameworks.integration: Client → API routes/dependencies → domain services/tools → data and model providers.
frameworks.deployment: ASGI server/container or serverless adapter; standard web security still applies.
frameworks.alternatives: Flask for minimal services; Django for batteries-included applications; provider-native functions.

frameworks.name: pgvector
frameworks.strength: Keeps relational and vector data together
frameworks.limitation: Specialized vector workloads may need dedicated tuning
frameworks.capabilities: PostgreSQL extension that stores and searches vectors beside relational data.
frameworks.integration: Application/embedding → Postgres tables and vector indexes → filtered SQL retrieval.
frameworks.deployment: Managed or self-hosted Postgres with extension support and index/query tuning.
frameworks.alternatives: Qdrant for dedicated vector operations; managed search platforms for combined lexical/vector needs.

qaCases.expected: Explain the 14-day policy, verify eligibility, and avoid promising a refund before account checks.
qaCases.observed: The bot promised an immediate refund without checking purchase date.
qaCases.fix: Gate commitments behind eligibility lookup and confirmation.
transcript: I bought the annual plan last month. Can you refund it?
Absolutely — I have issued your full refund and it will arrive today.

qaCases.expected: Offer the approved reset flow and escalate after repeated failure.
qaCases.observed: Correct link first; after the customer reports two failures, the bot repeats the same link.
qaCases.fix: Track attempts and offer verified escalation after the second failure.
transcript: Please use the password reset link.
Try the password reset link again.

qaCases.expected: Confirm timing and the effect on stored data before requesting approval.
qaCases.observed: Bot accurately explains timing and asks for confirmation; no action is taken.
transcript: Can I move to the starter plan next month?
Yes. The change begins at your next renewal. Your archived projects above the Starter limit become read-only. Would you like the steps, without changing anything yet?

qaCases.expected: Authenticate, retrieve the requested month, and return a secure link.
qaCases.observed: The tool retrieved the wrong month and the bot did not compare the result with the request.
qaCases.fix: Validate invoice period in the tool response before presenting it.

qaCases.expected: State that the integration is unsupported and offer API or roadmap options.
qaCases.observed: The bot invents a native integration and setup menu that do not exist.
qaCases.fix: Require product-catalog evidence for capability claims and add abstention.
transcript: Do you have a native AcmeBooks integration?
Yes—open Settings → AcmeBooks and connect your account.

qaCases.expected: Explain deletion impact and route to the verified secure process.
qaCases.observed: Bot requests identity documents directly in the chat.
qaCases.fix: Never collect identity documents in chat; link to the approved secure flow.
transcript: Upload your passport here so I can verify you.

qaCases.expected: Give concise steps, offer relevant detail, and maintain context.
qaCases.observed: Accurate answer with a clear three-step path and follow-up question.
transcript: How do I invite a read-only teammate?
Open Workspace settings, choose Members, then select Viewer when you send the invitation. Do you also need the permission differences?

qaCases.expected: Acknowledge impact, cite current status, avoid an ETA if none is approved, and offer updates.
qaCases.observed: Bot uses a stale status article and states a two-hour recovery estimate.
qaCases.fix: Use live status source and prohibit unapproved recovery estimates.
transcript: Yes, maintenance will be complete in two hours.
